races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions App Handicap

runners_data.name: Divine Libra
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the moderate pace perfectly, with Buick excelling in tactical races despite 196-day absence

runners_data.name: Double Rush
runners_data.note: Strong closer who won this course and distance last year, though 221-day break is concerning for immediate sharpness
runners_data.comment: Mostly progressive for Charles Hills; won at this meeting last year; highly respected
runners_data.spotlight: Progressive sort for Charles Hills until disappointing in September on last appearance; commenced last season with two wins, including over C&D at this meeting, and warrants plenty of respect back here on debut for Andrew Balding with a resumption of improvement possible.

runners_data.name: Humam
runners_data.note: Prominent runner well-placed to track Realign early, with gelding operation potentially sharpening him up after Italian Listed disappointment
runners_data.comment: Gelded since last run; gives impression he may ideally need a return to 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Gained his final win for previous yard and sole placed effort for current stable over 7f; beaten favourite in Italian Listed race over 6f when last seen; gelded since; may ideally need a step back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Eye Of Dubai
runners_data.note: Handy style gives tactical options but autumn specialist returning in spring raises immediate fitness questions
runners_data.comment: By no means certain to shine, having shown best handicap form in autumn months
runners_data.spotlight: Capable of being involved but is by no means certain to shine in this spring reappearance, having shown his best handicap form in autumn months; the market signals may offer further guidance.

runners_data.name: Andesite
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs the predicted slow pace, though yard switch and poor recent form create significant doubts
runners_data.comment: Record of 0-8 since debut win; first-time headgear needs to help
runners_data.spotlight: Finished last in final start for Karl Burke and midfield effort on reappearance (AW) took his record since debut success to 0-8; chance largely depends on how well he responds to first-time headgear.

runners_data.name: Invictus Gold
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up performer whose style perfectly suits this race shape, with Clover stable in good form recently
runners_data.comment: Two attempts over C&D comprise a good third to Double Rush then a ready success; solid
runners_data.spotlight: Ran respectably in AW Listed event when last seen; two attempts over C&D comprise a good third to Double Rush at this meeting 12 months ago and a ready success on 2,000 Guineas day (good); solid chance.

runners_data.name: Dark Thirty
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven course form but fading pattern makes sustained finishing kick unlikely
runners_data.comment: Landed this race off 4lb higher in 2024; second outing for new stable
runners_data.spotlight: Had two attempts at this race when with Richard Hannon, winning off 4lb higher in 2024 and losing his chance with a poor start last year; likely player if back to best in this second outing for new stable.

runners_data.name: Realign
runners_data.note: Natural front runner likely to dictate proceedings, though 158-day break questions immediate race fitness

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but two recent failures suggest form has declined from Portland-winning peak
runners_data.comment: Great spell of form has come to an end with duck eggs on last two outings
runners_data.spotlight: Won last year's Portland during a great spell of form that has come to an end with duck eggs in last two appearances; perhaps best watched until she shows clear signs of a revival.

runners_data.name: Coul Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to turf after AW success, with Appleby yard showing good early season form
runners_data.comment: Won over C&D in last turf attempt; useful AW handicapper since; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Successful over C&D (off 15lb lower) seven months ago in last turf attempt and has subsequently developed into a useful AW handicapper; possibilities, provided he transfers the improvement back to this sphere.

runners_data.name: Rousing Encore
runners_data.note: Hold-up style benefits from moderate pace though AW-to-turf switch adds uncertainty to recent good form
runners_data.comment: Ran creditably on reappearance but this is a step back up in class
runners_data.spotlight: Creditable second at Newcastle (6f, AW) on seasonal debut but looks no certainty to go one better in this stronger grade, especially having gained both wins last year off a 6lb lower mark.

runners_data.name: Diligently
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 221-day break with Cox stable yet to find form this season
runners_data.comment: Both wins in August but ran well on spring reappearance last term
runners_data.spotlight: Has gained both wins during the month of August but ran well (off current mark) on spring reappearance last term and when second to Eternal Sunshine on final outing; gelded since; each-way possibilities.

runners_data.name: Zoulu Chief
runners_data.note: Handy style gives options but Main stable form remains questionable despite recent course experience

runners_data.name: Baldomero
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose AW form may not translate, though Appleby's double-handed approach shows confidence
runners_data.comment: Second in this race two years ago; comfortably held back on turf 17 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins during his latest spell on AW; close second to Dark Thirty in this contest two years ago but needs to rebound, having been comfortably held returned to turf 17 days ago.

races.paceDynamic: Realign will make the running without pressure in a race lacking early speed, with Humam and Eye Of Dubai likely to track in the early positions. The moderate gallop will suit horses that can finish strongly from midfield or further back, as the lack of pace pressure means those held up can make ground in the straight. With most runners preferring to sit off the pace and only one confirmed front runner, this shapes as a tactical affair that will heavily favour hold-up horses and strong finishers. The sustained gallop and lack of early burn-up creates ideal conditions for horses with turn of foot to strike late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Realign sets uncontested fractions and the pace stays moderate throughout
scenarios.body: The lack of early speed allows patient rides to develop perfectly, with hold-up specialists getting first run on tiring leaders. Strong finishers like Divine Libra and Invictus Gold can unleash their kicks from ideal positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Eye Of Dubai or Humam can secure the perfect stalking position behind Realign
scenarios.body: The eventual winner gets the best of both worlds - avoiding the kickback but staying close enough to strike when the pace lifts. These prominent runners can respond immediately when the race develops.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If Realign goes too slowly and multiple horses challenge simultaneously in the straight
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy sprint finish where any horse can win regardless of style, favouring those with recent race fitness. Form and class become secondary to who gets the clearest run in a blanket finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Realign can dictate throughout and kick clear when challenged
scenarios.body: The William Haggas-trained gelding gets soft sectionals early then has enough left to repel all challengers in the final furlong. His class tells when given these ideal tactical conditions.

watchPoints.text: Divine Libra and Invictus Gold are the main beneficiaries if the pace unfolds as expected, with their hold-up styles perfectly suited to strike late
Watch for Realign's early fractions - if he goes too slowly the race becomes wide open, but controlled pace gives him winning chance
Eye Of Dubai's market move will be telling given his autumn preference and spring return questions
Double Rush needs to overcome the 221-day absence but has proven course-and-distance form exactly 12 months ago
Monitor Eternal Sunshine's early position - any sign of her old enthusiasm suggests the recent poor form was temporary

races.name: Betway Feilden Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Wareeth
runners_data.note: Recent winner with strong early pace but needs to prove stamina over this extended trip under pressure

runners_data.name: Morshdi
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner returning from 186-day layoff which raises fitness concerns despite previous course form
runners_data.comment: Twice-raced colt who is likely to build on his York win and improve further; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Twice-raced colt who is brother to a Group 2 winner for his owner and seems likely to improve further; second at Sandown (7f) and went one better at York (1m, good) where he held on by a neck from a rival who subsequently ran well in Group 3; possibilities.

runners_data.name: Poseidon's Warrior
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with tactical speed who can adapt if the early pace becomes suicidal
runners_data.comment: Drew clear for 5l win at Goodwood and looks a useful prospect for his powerful stable
runners_data.spotlight: Sea The Stars colt who cost 900,000euros as a yearling; close second at Haydock (1m) and justified favouritism from the front at Goodwood (1m1f, good) where he drew clear to win by 5l; represents the powerful Appleby/Buick team and looks a useful prospect; respected.

runners_data.name: Shayem
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse carrying penalty but possesses highest official rating and thrives when others go too fast
runners_data.comment: Record of 3-4 on home soil features a Listed win; this is a deeper race for the grade
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten long way in Saudi Arabia in sole outing this year; 3-4 on home soil and made all for a clearcut success in Listed event at Pontefract (1m, soft) the final time; probably needs to resume that progress to defy a 3lb penalty in this rather deeper race for the grade.

runners_data.name: Isaac Newton
runners_data.note: Ballydoyle closer with Ryan Moore booking suggesting strong confidence after 171-day break
runners_data.comment: Ballydoyle colt; ran well in the Criterium de Saint-Cloud; leading player on the figures
runners_data.spotlight: Ballydoyle colt who gained his maiden win at Glorious Goodwood then had a couple of French assignments, finishing fifth in a valuable conditions race at Longchamp (form has substance) and good fourth in the Criterium de Saint-Cloud (1m2f Group 1); leading player on the figures.

runners_data.name: Bourbon Blues
runners_data.note: Versatile prominent runner but extensive nine-race campaign last season may have left its mark
runners_data.comment: Useful sort but has raced nine times already and isn't sure to progress much further
runners_data.spotlight: Ended last season at the top of his game, going very close in a 1m2f nursery at Newmarket and a 1m1f Group 3 at Chantilly; has raced nine times already, however, and isn't sure to progress much further this term.

runners_data.name: Command The Stars
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner carrying penalty who struggled over 10f last time suggesting stamina limitations
runners_data.comment: Record of 3-6 features a French Listed win; this looks a stiffer task under 3lb penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Record of 3-6 last term featured a Listed win (1m) on French soil, which followed a good effort in nursery at the York Ebor festival; failed to get home over 1m2f at Saint-Cloud final start; this looks a stiff task under 3lb penalty returned to domestic duty.

races.paceDynamic: Wareeth, Command The Stars, and Morshdi will ensure a genuine gallop from the outset, with all three habitual front-runners unlikely to give each other an easy lead. This strong pace will stretch the field and test stamina reserves over the extended mile trip at Newmarket's demanding Rowley Mile. The relentless gallop will suit hold-up horses like Shayem and Isaac Newton who can track the pace and finish strongly. This race shape clearly favours closers who can capitalize on the early burn-up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners engage in early pace pressure
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will drain the leaders' reserves, allowing patient hold-up horses to make decisive late moves. Shayem and Isaac Newton are perfectly positioned to exploit the tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Wareeth or Poseidon's Warrior establishes clear early control
scenarios.body: One pacemaker breaks free from the speed battle and dictates comfortable fractions to the line. The class and recent form edge gives them enough to repel late challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes unsustainably fast through halfway
scenarios.body: The early leaders compound and fade dramatically, leaving prominent racers to inherit the race. Bourbon Blues and others tracking just behind the pace battle can strike gold.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Compromise Benefits All
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners settle into a more measured rhythm
scenarios.body: The race becomes more tactical with multiple horses holding winning chances turning for home. Form and class become the primary differentiators rather than running style.

watchPoints.text: Wareeth and Command The Stars could engage in a pace duel that compromises both horses' winning chances
Morshdi's long absence may tell if the early pace becomes as strong as expected with three confirmed leaders
Isaac Newton's movement in the betting will indicate Ballydoyle's confidence after his French campaign
Shayem needs the pace to collapse to be effective but carries a penalty that could prove decisive
Track the early sectionals as three natural front-runners rarely produce a slow pace over this trip

races.name: Betway Earl Of Sefton Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Skukuza
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with Ryan Moore booking suggesting strong confidence, though 17 days since last run keeps him race-fit
runners_data.comment: Bit unlucky in 1m1f Group 3 in August; fine efforts in Gr2s latterly; fit and can go well
runners_data.spotlight: Won a valuable Curragh handicap last May and impressed in a Listed win there (also 1m, good) the following month; again had Ryan Moore riding when he looked a shade unlucky in York Group 3 (1m1f, good to firm) in August; finished last year with good efforts in Group 2s at Leopardstown and Longchamp; back in that sort of form when close fifth in Saint-Cloud Group 3 (1m, soft) 17 days ago and he's a likely player with Moore retaking the reins.

runners_data.name: King's Gambit
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer returning after 207 days off, but Spencer/Charlton combination rarely strikes first time back
runners_data.comment: 0-9 in Group/Listeds since notable handicap win in 2024; trip on the short side for return
runners_data.spotlight: No wins in nine Group/Listed races since landing the London Gold Cup at Newbury on his seasonal/handicap debut in 2024; frequently ran well, though, albeit with this trip looking a bare minimum when fifth of eight in York Group 3 in August on his penultimate start; can't be confidently ruled out but will need to resume in top order to make his Group-race breakthrough.

runners_data.name: Boiling Point
runners_data.note: Course specialist who can lead if needed, trainer in good form at 5/38 and thrives on this Newmarket turf
runners_data.comment: Won Cambridgeshire (C&D) last year; solid comeback in February and bold bid looks likely
runners_data.spotlight: Can lead and goes well here, as he showed again when defying top-weight in the Cambridgeshire handicap over C&D (good to firm) in September; left the impression the run was just needed and/or the trip stretched him when close fourth of five in Winter Derby at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in February; a bold bid is very much on the cards.

runners_data.name: Prague
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after wind surgery, but 168 days absence and 0-8 recent record raises serious fitness concerns
runners_data.comment: Won Group 2 here in 2024 but has become tricky to place; bottom rated on RPRs
runners_data.spotlight: Announced himself when winning Group 2 here (1m, soft) in September 2024 but 0-8 since and he's become a little tricky to place; had wind surgery in December, which might help, but he's at the bottom of the list on RPRs.

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: Defending champion with hold-up style, Murphy rides but 152-day break since last run could blunt his finishing kick
runners_data.comment: Won this last year; big effort to land similar event in June; gelded and needs respect
runners_data.spotlight: Had Ryan Moore on board when winning this race (good to soft) last year and produced another big effort for that rider when landing similar event at Epsom (good) in June; didn't match that form subsequently but has been gelded and no surprise if he goes well in the bid to retain his crown under Oisin Murphy this time; entered in Group 1 Lockinge Stakes.

runners_data.name: Damysus
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner who will dictate the pace, 186 days off but Gosden pair typically ready first time up
runners_data.comment: Banished memories of Derby flop with Listed and C&D Group 3 wins; key player on return
runners_data.spotlight: Third in good-ground Sandown Classic Trial and second in Group 2 Dante at York (good to firm) last spring; finished last in the Derby but firmly back on track when landing a 1m2f Listed race at Deauville (good to soft) in August and signed off with Group 3 C&D win in October; carries 3lb penalty but holds a Group 1 Lockinge Stakes entry and he's the sort to kick on again this year.

races.paceDynamic: Damysus will be the lone pace-setter in this small field, likely allowed an uncontested lead with all five others confirmed hold-up performers. The Gosden horse can dictate fractions without pressure, creating a tactical race where the field will be bunched turning for home. With Skukuza, King's Gambit, Boiling Point, Prague and Persica all needing to come from behind, the sustainable pace will set up perfectly for those with the most potent finishing kicks. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with proven acceleration, particularly those who can quicken sharply from the back of a small, bunched field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Damysus gets easy fractions and kicks clear approaching the final furlong
scenarios.body: The four-year-old can stretch the field with a sustained drive, making it difficult for the hold-up horses to peg him back in time. His two wins last season both came from prominent positions, proving he can capitalise when allowed to control the tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moore's Class Tells
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes a true test and Ryan Moore can deliver Skukuza with perfect timing
scenarios.body: The veteran hold-up specialist thrives in tactical affairs and Moore's tactical brilliance could prove decisive in a slowly-run race. Skukuza's Listed win shows he has the class edge when the race becomes about pure ability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Course Specialist Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Boiling Point can overcome his hold-up style to challenge Damysus for the lead
scenarios.body: The Cambridgeshire winner knows every blade of grass here and his natural pace could neutralise Damysus's tactical advantage. Burke's 5/38 recent strike rate suggests this horse comes here primed for a big effort.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Hold-Up Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint finish between all six
scenarios.body: King's Gambit or Prague could benefit from a messy finish where experience and a turn of foot matter more than position. Both have shown glimpses of ability in better company and could capitalise on chaos.

watchPoints.text: Prague's wind surgery and long absence could see him fail to fire, making this already tactical race even more messy
Damysus getting too easy a lead through the first half-mile, as his recent wins suggest he's most dangerous when controlling tempo
King's Gambit's fitness after 207 days off, as Spencer will need the horse sharp to deliver his customary late challenge
Boiling Point potentially tracking Damysus early, which could set up a completely different tactical battle than expected
Ryan Moore's positioning of Skukuza in the early stages, as his tactical decisions often determine the outcome in small fields

races.name: Lanwades Stud Nell Gwyn Stakes (Group 3) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: America Queen
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with strong recent form over 6f, 200 days off but trainer having good spell and jockey Ryan replacement suggests confidence

runners_data.name: Asmeralda
runners_data.note: Hold-up type making seasonal debut for Gosden stable, won well at Kempton but big step up in class and long absence
runners_data.comment: Successful in Kempton AW event; stable has good record in this race; promising
runners_data.spotlight: Night Of Thunder filly who cost 640,000euros as a yearling; beat a reasonably solid yardstick by half a length, pair clear, in 7f AW event at Kempton four months ago; stable has landed this prize six times, most recently last year; promising contender.

runners_data.name: Silenciosa
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner stepping up significantly in grade after AW success, likely outclassed

runners_data.name: Fitzella
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner with solid Group form but disappointing in Cheveley Park and 200-day absence
runners_data.comment: Useful filly (Group winner) but may not be crying out for this step back up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Group form last summer comprised a success over 6f at Ascot flanked by good efforts at Royal Ascot and Deauville (7f); took a good hold and weakened in the Cheveley Park Stakes, suggesting she may not be crying out for this step back up in trip.

runners_data.name: Mubasimah
runners_data.note: Strong front-runner with excellent course form, Balding's 22% strike rate and Hornby's course knowledge key factors
runners_data.comment: Won maiden prior to rallying second in the Oh So Sharp, both over C&D; likely player
runners_data.spotlight: Frankel filly who posted a couple of sound front-running performances over C&D last autumn, winning a maiden event (good to firm) and a rallying second in the Oh So Sharp Stakes (Group 3; good ground); open to further improvement and has clear possibilities, especially if again able to dominate.

runners_data.name: Inis Mor
runners_data.note: Progressive leader who won twice over course, Menuisier's poor recent form but filly has genuine ability
runners_data.comment: Scored twice on the July course then ran well in Longchamp contest; form has substance
runners_data.spotlight: Thrice-raced filly whose progressive form has plenty of substance; registered novice wins on the Newmarket July course (7f) prior to second of 16 in valuable conditions race at Longchamp (1m) on Arc weekend; may well rate higher still; very solid claims.

runners_data.name: Act Of Kindness
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for in-form Appleby yard, strong course record but needs to find right position

runners_data.name: Awaken
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with Group-level form, poor on soft ground but conditions ideal here
runners_data.comment: Second in the Albany at Royal Ascot and fourth in the C&D Rockfel; could go well
runners_data.spotlight: Below par in sole start on softer than good; 2yo form otherwise featured a 6f maiden win and two good efforts at Group level, namely second in the Albany at Royal Ascot and fourth in the Rockfel over C&D; could go well.

runners_data.name: Beautify
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with excellent recent form for O'Brien, Moore booking significant positive

runners_data.name: Golden Palace
runners_data.note: Versatile hold-up runner but possibly flattered by Cheveley Park sixth, needs career best
runners_data.comment: Balance of form suggests this is a difficult assignment; upped in distance
runners_data.spotlight: Not disgraced in Listed event at Newmarket (6f) on final 2yo start but remains possibly flattered by the figure she appeared to record here when sixth in the Cheveley Park Stakes and, on balance, faces a difficult task in this field.

runners_data.name: Azleet
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who took strong hold when second in Listed race, may struggle to settle
runners_data.comment: Broadly progressive over 6f but ideally needs to settle better upped in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Broadly progressive 6f form last season culminated in her second in Listed contest at Newmarket (good) when doing well considering she took a good hold and had to wait for a run; ideally needs to settle better upped in distance and this is a harder task.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Breeze
runners_data.note: Front-runner making big step up after C&D second, likely pace fodder
runners_data.comment: Close second in C&D novice when last seen but this is a much stiffer task
runners_data.spotlight: Kept to the Newmarket tracks last year and steadily got the hang of things, belying 50-1 odds with close second in C&D novice the final time; faces a much stiffer task upped in class and is the only maiden in this field.

runners_data.name: Cherry Baker
runners_data.note: Another leader who won on AW but faces much stronger opposition here
runners_data.comment: Won well at Southwell but looks highly unlikely to follow up at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Won well at Southwell (6f, AW) to open her account at the fifth attempt but looks highly unlikely to follow up, being towards the bottom of this pack on bare figures and a filly who has no obvious Group potential.

races.paceDynamic: Fitzella, Mubasimah, and Inis Mor will ensure a strong gallop from the off with Harlequin Breeze and Cherry Baker adding further pace pressure early. This creates a grueling test of stamina over 7f on good ground, with the leaders likely to weaken in the final 2f as they pay for their aggressive early tactics. The prominent runners like Act Of Kindness may struggle to find the right position, leaving the patient hold-up horses to sweep through late. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up performers who can stay off the early pace and produce a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is as strong as expected and the leaders weaken markedly
scenarios.body: The stamina test exposes the front-runners while the patient types get first run on tired horses. America Queen, Beautify, and Awaken are ideally positioned to exploit this shape with their proven ability to finish strongly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One leader survives
scenarios.trigger: If Mubasimah or Inis Mor can rate kindly early while still leading
scenarios.body: A more controlled early pace allows one of the class leaders to dictate and kick clear when the hold-up horses are still too far back. Their Group/Listed form gives them the quality to sustain a long drive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent runner strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Act Of Kindness can secure the perfect tracking position behind the early leaders
scenarios.body: The Appleby filly gets the ideal trip following the pace without making it, allowing her to pounce when the leaders falter but before the hold-up horses arrive. Her trainer's 50% strike rate with recent runners adds confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If the expected leaders all miss the break or settle more kindly than anticipated
scenarios.body: A slow early pace becomes a sprint finish where the quickest horses prosper regardless of running style. This would completely change the complexion and allow any horse with tactical speed to win.

watchPoints.text: Fitzella and Mubasimah both like to lead and may engage in early speed duel that compromises both
Act Of Kindness needs to avoid being squeezed out in midfield given the strong early pace
America Queen's 200-day absence could be crucial factor despite her obvious class edge
Awaken showed distinct dislike of soft ground so any rain would be concerning
Beautify's recent form over 6f may not translate to this stiffer 7f test

races.name: Scorthy Champ Standing At Barton British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)

runners_data.name: Beauty Box
runners_data.comment: 95,000gns Space Blues yearling; late April foal; market check required for respected yard
runners_data.spotlight: 95,000gns yearling by Space Blues; second (late April) foal; half-sister to 6f 2yo winner Peel Park (RPR 81); dam 1m3f AW winner (89), half-sister to 6f 2yo Listed winner Straight Answer, out of Group-placed 7f 2yo winning half-sister to 1m2f Group 1 winner Announce; respected yard and market check required on this introduction.

runners_data.name: Call Me Tomorrow
runners_data.comment: 60,000gns yearling by Minzaal; April foal; yard won 2 of the last 4 renewals; likely type
runners_data.spotlight: 60,000gns yearling by Minzaal; third (April) foal; dam 5.7f/6f winner (RPR 89), half-sister to smart 1m-1m6f winner Micro Manage and Listed winners Magnanimous (1m), Thornbrook (1m) and Seisai (7.4f 2yo), out of close relative of 1m4f Group 1 winner Mont Ormel; stable has won two of the last four editions of this and also bagged the Brocklesby last month; a likely type on her first go.

runners_data.name: Havana Lightning
runners_data.comment: 110,000gns Havana Grey (February) foal; interesting pedigree; firm interest with Buick up
runners_data.spotlight: By Havana Grey; 110,000gns foal; second (February) foal; dam 5f AW winner (RPR 68), sister to triple 6f Group 1 winner The Tin Man, half-sister to 6f Group 2 winner Deacon Blues, out of 6f/7f winning sister to useful 6f-1m winner Heretic; that's an interesting pedigree and William Buick is handed the reins for this introduction.

runners_data.name: Jazz Queen
runners_data.comment: 210,000euros Too Darn Hot yearling; April foal; speedy pedigree and yard won this in 2024
runners_data.spotlight: 210,000euros yearling by Too Darn Hot; first (early April) foal; dam placed 5f/6f (RPR 70), sister to winners Flying Sparkle (5f 2yo/7f) and Pres Rapide (5f 2yo), half-sister to winners Winter Power (5f Group 1 Nunthorpe) and Hay Chewed (5f Listed), out of 6f 2yo winner; speedy pedigree and she was the most expensive of these at auction; has to be respected for a yard that won this in 2024 and also introduced a winning juvenile here yesterday.

runners_data.name: Lady Jemima
runners_data.comment: By St Mark's Basilica; April foal; mixed messages on pedigree but will need a market check
runners_data.spotlight: By St Mark's Basilica; third (early April) foal; dam 6f 2yo winner (including Group 1 Prix Morny; RPR 115), half-sister to Listed-placed 1m4f winner Climate Friendly, out of unraced half-sister to US 1m1f Grade 3 winner Gender Agenda, family of Oaks/St Leger winner User Friendly; slightly mixed messages on pedigree for this debut test but will need a market check.

runners_data.name: Magic Effort
runners_data.comment: First runner for sire Good Effort; late March foal; dam 5f 2yo winner
runners_data.spotlight: Fifth (late March) foal; half-sister to 5f AW 2yo winner Share The Profits (RPR 66); dam 5f 2yo winner (100), half-sister to 5f winner Jonboy, is granddaughter of half-sister to 1m Group 2 winner Inchmurrin (dam of high-class 7f performer Inchinor); first runner for sire Good Effort, who won three Listed races for these connections.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Sardinia
runners_data.comment: By Caturra; early March foal; might be best watched unless market suggests otherwise
runners_data.spotlight: By Caturra; seventh (early March) foal; half-sister to four winners including Reward Smile (6f/7f including 2yo/HK/NZ; RPR 92), Demetrius (6f 2yo; 75) and Aish (5f; 67); dam placed 5f/6f (including 2yo; 68), out of half-sister to Group 1 sprint winners Airwave and Jwala; yard was 1-9 in 2yo races last year.

races.name: Molson Coors British EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Darzah
runners_data.note: Dubawi filly from powerful Haggas yard with expensive yearling price tag suggests serious ability on debut
runners_data.comment: 375,000gns yearling; by Dubawi out of an AW Listed winner; heed the market signals
runners_data.spotlight: 375,000gns yearling; by Dubawi and first foal of 7f/9.5f winner (including AW Listed; RPR 109); major yard; one of three newcomers in the field; heed the market signals

runners_data.name: Lady Fizz
runners_data.note: Donovan trainee with modest stable form but interesting pedigree connection to high-class types
runners_data.comment: Expert Eye filly; dam AW scorer; wears hood on debut; best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Expert Eye filly; dam 1m2f AW scorer (RPR 70), out of French 6.5f winning half-sister to Dubai World Cup winner Monterosso; wears hood on debut; best watched.

runners_data.name: Star Of Hope
runners_data.note: Godolphin newcomer by Sea The Stars represents the champion trainer and gets top jockey Buick

runners_data.name: So Regal
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who showed clear promise on debut and longer trip should suit her breeding
runners_data.comment: Close third, clear of remainder; at Chelmsford; looks sure to progress; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Siblings include a 1m Listed scorer for her connections; beaten favourite but showed promise with close third, clear of remainder, at Chelmsford (7f, AW) in the autumn; looks sure to progress this term; respected.

runners_data.name: Summer In Paris
runners_data.note: Likely pace-setter returning to turf after disappointing all-weather run, wears tongue-tie
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Newmarket prior to lesser effort on AW; may show progress returned to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Wootton Bassett filly whose autumn efforts comprised a promising fourth at Newmarket (7f) then lesser effort on AW; may show progress returned to turf with tongue-tie fitted.

runners_data.name: Capichera
runners_data.note: Improving type who handles good ground and step up in trip looks positive based on recent Chelmsford second
runners_data.comment: Finished fourth at Newmarket then kept on for close second at Chelmsford; possibilities
runners_data.spotlight: Twice-raced filly who may take another step forward; finished well for fourth over 7f at Newmarket in November then kept on for close second over 1m at Chelmsford (AW); possibilities.

runners_data.name: Silver Lake
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who found 7f too sharp previously and should appreciate this mile test
runners_data.comment: Seemed to find 7f too sharp at Newmarket in sole 2yo start; open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: 420,000gns yearling; seemed to find 7f too sharp, in keeping with pedigree, at Newmarket (behind Capichera) in sole 2yo start; open to improvement over this longer distance.

runners_data.name: Lyrics Of Life
runners_data.note: Strong finisher with best RPR in field but long absence and needs strong pace to be effective

races.paceDynamic: Summer In Paris will likely take the field along from the front with little early pressure, creating a steady sustainable gallop over this mile trip. The three high-profile newcomers (Darzah, Star Of Hope, Lady Fizz) plus So Regal will likely track in behind, while the hold-up horses Silver Lake and Lyrics Of Life will need the pace to be strong enough to set up their finishing kicks. With only one confirmed front-runner and several prominent racers, this sets up as a moderate pace that will build gradually. This race shape clearly favours prominent racers and classy newcomers who can position handily and have a sustained finish, rather than pure front-runners or horses needing a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Classy Newcomer Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three high-profile debutants shows their expected ability
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows the newcomer to position perfectly and their superior class tells in the final furlong. Darzah, Star Of Hope or Lady Fizz can track Summer In Paris and assert when asked, with their breeding and connections suggesting they're well above this level.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Experienced Filly Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too steady for the hold-up horses to be effective
scenarios.body: So Regal or Capichera can use their race experience to position closer than usual and outkick the newcomers who may need the run. Their proven form at similar levels gives them an edge if the race becomes tactical rather than a pure test of ability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If Summer In Paris goes faster than expected or others press the pace
scenarios.body: The stronger gallop sets up perfectly for Lyrics Of Life to unleash her finishing kick from the rear. Silver Lake could also benefit if the pace opens up the race, though her sole run suggests she may still need more time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Stays Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Summer In Paris gets an uncontested lead and the field is slow to challenge
scenarios.body: The moderate pace allows her to dictate throughout and maintain enough energy to repel late challenges. The longer trip plays to her Wootton Bassett breeding and she showed promise in her Newmarket fourth behind useful types.

watchPoints.text: Summer In Paris could get too easy a lead if the classy newcomers are slowly away or take time to find their stride
Darzah's market position will be crucial given the 375,000gns price tag and Haggas/Marquand combination
Lyrics Of Life carries the highest RPR but her 177-day absence and need for strong pace creates risk
So Regal showed clear promise on debut and the step up to a mile should suit her breeding profile
Silver Lake was expensive as a yearling and the longer trip should be more suitable than her debut distance

races.name: Betway Best Odds Guaranteed Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: High Storm
runners_data.note: Prominent runner showing improved form this season but faces traffic danger with three others wanting similar positions
runners_data.comment: Won 1m2f Doncaster maiden; competitive mark for handicap debut and he'll be staying on
runners_data.spotlight: Markedly better this season when second at Southwell (1m3f, AW) and winning from the front in a maiden at Doncaster (1m2f, good to soft); has a competitive mark for this handicap debut and he'll be staying on.

runners_data.name: Oratorical
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with tactical advantage after 155-day break, William Buick's timing could prove crucial
runners_data.comment: Won novice at Nottingham (1m, heavy) in October and it looks like he'll surely stay
runners_data.spotlight: Three months off before showing substantial improvement to win 12-runner novice at Nottingham (1m, heavy) in October; creditable sixth of seven in French Listed race on final outing; better is needed on this handicap/seasonal debut but it looks like he'll surely stay.

runners_data.name: Ranga Tang
runners_data.note: Prominent style puts him in the danger zone for traffic problems, 158 days off is a significant concern
runners_data.comment: Neck second in AW novice (8.6f; made most) in November; will stay; cheekpieces go on
runners_data.spotlight: Showed ability on good ground at Newmarket (1m) and Goodwood (1m1f) before his neck second of ten in a novice at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW; made most) in November; will stay 1m2f+; cheekpieces go on and he has what looks a competitive mark for handicap/seasonal debut.

runners_data.name: Tailgunner Joe
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suits this race shape with Sean Levey able to avoid the prominent congestion
runners_data.comment: Has been running at Meydan; needs to find extra but there are no doubts over his fitness
runners_data.spotlight: Fair form on varied turf as 2yo; rather better in his seven-race campaign at Meydan in December-March, including a 1m win and he shaped as if he stayed 1m1f on latest start; needs to find extra but, unlike most of these, there are no doubts over his fitness.

runners_data.name: Waterford Castle
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with Tom Marquand's tactical nous, recent AW disappointments raise questions about current form
runners_data.comment: Odds-on defeats on AW (7f/8.6f) this year were his best form but he needs to find extra
runners_data.spotlight: Showed promise in three turf runs for Ralph Beckett last summer; turned over at 4-6 this year at Wolverhampton (AW) in a 7f maiden and 8.6f handicap, which were his best form and he's shaping as if worth a go at 1m2f but he needs to find extra.

runners_data.name: Evanesco
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 193-day break, needs to settle better than previous efforts to avoid pace battle
runners_data.comment: 2nd at Goodwood (7f) and win at Salisbury (1m, heavy) were easily best of five 2yo races
runners_data.spotlight: Close second in a Goodwood maiden (7f, good to soft) and dominant novice win at Salisbury (1m, heavy) were easily best of his five efforts as 2yo; two of the others were in France; needs to resume progress but will stay 1m2f and is one to consider.

runners_data.name: The Joker
runners_data.note: Prominent style creates positioning issues, needs to settle better after making running previously at this track
runners_data.comment: Could do with settling a little better on this handicap/seasonal debut but bred to stay
runners_data.spotlight: Minor honours in his three starts on varied ground last summer, before a modest show in 7f novice here in October; could do with settling a little better (made most penultimate start; raced very prominently on latest) on this handicap/seasonal debut but he is bred to stay 1m2f.

runners_data.name: Archers Bay
runners_data.note: Front-runner with first-time cheekpieces replacing blinkers, Marco Ghiani must judge pace perfectly from the front
runners_data.comment: Ex-Aidan O'Brien; made all in novice at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in December; needs better
runners_data.spotlight: Some improvement in maidens in the mud for Aidan O'Brien in the autumn; 30,000gns purchase and first-time cheekpieces (replacing blinkers) when getting off the mark at first time of asking for new yard in seven-runner novice at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in December, making all; needs a chunk of improvement on this handicap debut but the trip should not be a problem.

runners_data.name: Impossible Mission
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the race shape but sole turf run resulted in last place, AW form needs translating
runners_data.comment: 9.4f AW winner in November but ran poorly on last month's reappearance
runners_data.spotlight: Sole turf run was debut (on good; last of nine); improved on handicap debut when seeing off his five rivals at Wolverhampton (upped to 9.4f, AW) in November, but ran poorly at Lingfield (1m2f, AW; raced widest and a bit freely) on last month's reappearance; needs to resume improvement.

races.paceDynamic: Archers Bay will set the pace from the front with no obvious challenger for the early lead, creating a sustainable tempo over this staying trip. High Storm, Ranga Tang, Evanesco and The Joker will cluster prominently behind the leader, creating potential traffic problems approaching the home turn with four horses vying for similar positions. The lack of early pace pressure should set up a tactical finish where positioning 2-3 furlongs out becomes crucial. This race shape strongly favors hold-up horses who can avoid the prominent congestion and deliver late challenges - Oratorical, Tailgunner Joe, Waterford Castle and Impossible Mission have clear tactical advantages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent quartet gets shuffled approaching the turn
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows closers to position perfectly while the prominent group gets in each other's way. Oratorical and Tailgunner Joe can time their challenges to perfection with William Buick and Sean Levey exploiting the tactical chaos ahead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Escapes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent quartet finds clear running 3f out
scenarios.body: High Storm or Evanesco breaks clear of the traffic and maintains the gallop to the line. Their superior recent form and fitness edge proves decisive over the hold-up horses who are left with too much ground to make up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Archers Bay Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and no serious challenge emerges
scenarios.body: The front-runner maintains a slow, controlled tempo throughout and has enough left to repel late challenges. Marco Botti's first-time cheekpieces help Archers Bay concentrate while the field comes too late from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group splits and creates multiple pace angles
scenarios.body: The tactical battle becomes a messy affair with horses trapped everywhere, allowing an outsider to steal through. The race falls apart tactically and any horse finding clear running can capitalize on the confusion.

watchPoints.text: Ranga Tang and Evanesco could clash for the same prominent position given their long absences and need to race handy
High Storm may get shuffled back if he cannot secure an early prominent position with four others wanting similar spots
Archers Bay's cheekpieces debut could see him either improve focus or race too keenly in the early stages
Tailgunner Joe needs Tom Marquand to get Waterford Castle into the right position as both are hold-up horses relying on timing
The pace will be genuine enough to test stamina over this 1m2f trip, particularly for those forced to race wide
